…mented ingester protocol (#1609)

Maps the engine's monitor event stream to standard OTel telemetry with
zero engine/server changes — the client-side refinement invited by
tracking issue #616 after the engine-invasive #498 was archived.

- mapper.py: stateful FlowSpanMapper reconstructs span trees from
  apaevt_flow — task root span, pipe span per pipe id, component child
  spans paired by component identity (per the observability doc's
  warning against stack-position pairing); trace.error -> span status
  ERROR + exception event; apaevt_sse -> span events; unclosed spans at
  end/shutdown flagged rocketride.span.unclosed=true; per-pipe state is
  bounded. MetricsMapper maps apaevt_status_update snapshots to OTel
  instruments (object counts, rates, cpu/gpu memory + peaks).
- Semantic conventions per the July 2026 semantic-conventions-genai
  snapshot: gen_ai.provider.name (not the deprecated gen_ai.system),
  gen_ai.operation.name from the well-known list only, span names
  '{operation} {model}' style, INTERNAL span kind for in-process
  component executions.
- Privacy by default: lane payloads / prompt / result content never
  reach attributes or events unless include_content is set (8KB
  truncation cap when it is); enforced by a sentinel-scan test across
  all exported attributes and events.
- setup.py: TracerProvider/MeterProvider + OTLP http/protobuf exporters;
  ALL opentelemetry imports are lazy so the base package imports without
  the extra.

53 unit tests (InMemorySpanExporter/InMemoryMetricReader; importorskip
so the base CI matrix stays green), including a full replay of the
captured real-engine event fixture.

…#1609)

rocketride otel [--endpoint URL] [--protocol http|grpc] [--service-name]
[--headers k=v,...] [--include-content] [--no-metrics] + the standard
connection args. Subscribes via rrext_monitor with token '*' (the
observability doc's recommended ingestion scope, types TASK|SUMMARY|
FLOW|SSE), dispatches to the mappers, reconnects with capped backoff
and resubscribes (subscriptions are per-connection and not durable),
and flushes exporters on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Endpoint resolution honors the standard OTLP env contract: explicit
--endpoint > OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT (verbatim) >
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (base URL + /v1/traces|/v1/metrics) >
default. Packaging: opentelemetry-sdk + OTLP http exporter live behind
an optional extra — the base install gains zero dependencies, and
running the subcommand without the extra exits 2 with the exact
"pip install 'rocketride[otel]'" hint before any connection attempt.

25 tests: config precedence matrix, dispatch/reconnect/resubscribe with
a fake client, shutdown flush ordering, missing-extra exit path.

…otion, header precedence, shutdown ordering

CodeRabbit review round on #1612, each finding verified before acting:

- mapper: trace.error no longer bypasses the privacy gate — by default
  only the error signal exports (status ERROR, bare exception event,
  generic description); --include-content restores verbatim text, now
  subject to the same 8KB truncation strings previously skipped. The
  sentinel privacy test plants the sentinel in trace.error.
- mapper: a run first seen via flow events (before the task 'running'
  snapshot) is now promoted from its project|source fallback key to the
  canonical run id when it arrives — previously a second run state was
  created (broken parentage) and the orphaned fallback state leaked
  permanently. Confirmed with a failing repro; guard test ensures two
  distinct canonical runs sharing (project, source) never merge.
- config/setup: only --headers become explicit exporter headers; env
  headers are left to the SDK so OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS /
  _METRICS_HEADERS signal precedence works (it was silently defeated).
  Precedence matrix tests added.
- setup: meter provider shutdown wrapped in finally so metrics flush
  even when tracer shutdown raises.
- CLI: --trace-level none message now says flow tracing stays disabled;
  docs recipes pass collector auth via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS env
  instead of argv (shell-history hygiene); error-mapping doc wording
  matches the implementation (component leave events).

…cedes it

Follow-on to the run-promotion fix: an SSE event creates the canonical
run state WITHOUT registering the (project, source) alias (SSE bodies
carry no project/source per the protocol), so an id-less flow for the
same run could still open a parallel fallback-keyed state — and because
the canonical state already existed, the promotion branch was skipped,
stranding the fallback state (kept alive forever by snapshot
reconciliation) with duplicate spans.

_get_run now reconciles whenever an event carries both the canonical id
and project/source: no canonical state → promote (unchanged); canonical
state exists → _absorb_fallback_run migrates non-colliding pipes (open
spans re-stamped with the canonical run id), closes colliding pipes as
rocketride.span.unclosed=true, and drops the fallback key. Only
fallback-format keys are touched, so distinct canonical runs never
merge (guard test unchanged and green).

Both new regression tests failed before the fix. Full extra: 92 passed;
partial install: 71 passed + expected skip; ruff clean.

commits.messageBody:
The bridge was written against a monitor protocol that carried no event
timestamps, so every span used the bridge's own clock at event arrival and
the guide documented that as a limitation. Since #1661 the engine stamps
`body.eventTime` (epoch seconds, set once at ingress by the run-log
continuum) on every forwarded event, and derived flow events inherit their
source event's stamp — so the limitation is no longer true and the
documentation shipped with it was wrong against develop.

Span start/end and span-event timestamps now come from `body.eventTime`,
making durations engine-measured instead of bridge-observed: WebSocket
transport latency and event-loop scheduling no longer inflate every
component span.

The fallback is exactly the previous behaviour. A body with no usable
`eventTime` (an older engine, or a non-float/NaN/non-positive value) and
every span closed outside an event — shutdown, seeded-snapshot
reconciliation, tracked-run cap eviction — use `time.time_ns()`, the same
clock the SDK would have used. Because a run can therefore mix both
sources, each open span records its own start and a close is clamped to
never precede it, so no span can report a negative duration.

Metric points are unchanged: OpenTelemetry metric instruments take no
explicit timestamp, so they remain arrival-timed. That is now stated
rather than left implicit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

packages/client-python/docs/index.md is the site's Python page and mirrors

The guide's ## Limitations still said span timestamps are arrival time
because the wire carries none; the previous commit made spans engine-timed,
so that bullet now describes what actually remains bridge-timed (spans
closed outside an event, pre-continuum engines, and all metric points).

The Python blocks in the guide are also reformatted: ruff formats Markdown
code blocks as of 0.16, and CI's ruff-action is unpinned, so the file failed

commits.messageBody:
Nine threads on the rebased head, all in the OTel bridge. Dispositions:

- docs/otel-bridge.md:151 (Sensitive Data Exposure, CWE-522) — FIXED. The
  Langfuse and LangSmith recipes now prompt for the keys (printf + read -rs,
  spelled identically in bash and zsh) instead of embedding placeholders that
  operators replace with live secrets in a command line, and point at a secret
  manager as the better source. The base64 pipeline is now
  `printf '%s' ... | base64 | tr -d '\r\n'`: real Langfuse keys make the
  joined string 85 characters, past GNU base64's 76-character wrap, and
  command substitution strips only trailing newlines, so the embedded break
  would have produced an invalid Authorization header.

- cli/commands/otel.py:207 (Sensitive Data Exposure, CWE-532) — FIXED. The
  startup line ran `config.endpoint` straight to stdout; an endpoint can carry
  userinfo credentials or a signed query string. It is now always passed
  through `redact_endpoint()`, which drops userinfo, query and fragment while
  keeping scheme/host/port and the ingest path operators actually verify.

- cli/main.py:466, otelbridge/config.py:177, otelbridge/setup.py:123
  (Cleartext Transmission, CWE-319) — FIXED, once, in one place.
  `validate_transport_security()` runs before any exporter exists (in
  `build_providers`, and again in the CLI so the failure is exit code 2 rather
  than a traceback): a credential-looking header name from `--headers` or any
  of the three OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*HEADERS variables, plus a non-loopback
  cleartext endpoint for either signal, aborts startup. Header VALUES are
  never read or echoed — only names reach the message. Loopback stays exempt
  for local collectors; `--insecure` / ROCKETRIDE_OTEL_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 is the
  explicit opt-out and warns on stderr.

- otelbridge/config.py:189 (CWE-201, redirect header forwarding) — FIXED. The
  OTLP/HTTP exporters now get a session that never follows redirects.
  `requests` strips Authorization only when the redirect changes host, so a
  3xx replayed x-api-key to the target and even kept Authorization on an
  https -> http downgrade to the same host.

- otelbridge/config.py:177 (endpoint precedence) — FIXED. `from_args_env` no
  longer pre-reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT into an explicit exporter
  endpoint: doing so overrode the signal-specific _TRACES_ENDPOINT /
  _METRICS_ENDPOINT, inverting the OTLP spec order — the same defect already
  fixed for the header variables in c23b3125. The SDK now resolves all three,
  and `effective_endpoint()` mirrors its order read-only for the startup line
  and the security check.

- otelbridge/bridge.py:207 (signal ownership) — FIXED. `loop.add_signal_handler`
  replaces rather than chains, and asyncio exposes no way to restore the
  displaced callback, so the bridge no longer touches a signal the running
  loop already handles; `install_signal_handlers=False` turns registration off
  entirely for embedders.

- otelbridge/mapper.py:611 (unbounded run.pipes) — FIXED. MAX_TRACKED_RUNS did
  not bound pipes: a run that keeps receiving events is re-inserted as
  most-recently-eventful and never evicted, while every begin (or event for a
  never-begun pipe) adds a _PipeState that only a matching end removes, and a
  reconnect does not replay missed ends. MAX_TRACKED_PIPES_PER_RUN now closes
  the least-recently-eventful pipe as unclosed, with recency updated on pipe
  activity rather than inferred from insertion order.

- otelbridge/setup.py:202 (tracer leak) — FIXED. A failure anywhere in the
  metric half left the BatchSpanProcessor worker running with no handle to
  stop it, because `shutdown` had not been created yet. That path now shuts
  the tracer provider down before re-raising.

Tests: 32 added (131 in tests/test_otel_*.py, was 99), covering stdout
redaction, the refusal and its opt-out, env-var and signal-specific endpoint
coverage, the non-redirecting session, the tracer teardown, signal ownership
and the pipe cap's LRU behaviour.

latestReviews.body:
The failure mode a telemetry bridge actually dies of is unbounded growth from spans that never close, and it is handled: caps on tracked runs and on pipes within a run, least-recently-eventful eviction, unclosed spans tagged `rocketride.span.unclosed=true` before being dropped, and content truncated at 8192 characters and only carried when asked for. The mapper has 999 lines of test behind it with real fixtures.

Additive — with no bridge configured nothing changes — and it speaks the ingester protocol that is already documented, so the claim of zero engine changes holds.

Approving on the engineering. Whether RocketRide wants to carry a fourth new CLI subcommand is a product call, not a review one, and it is worth making that call before this lands: it shares `cli.mdx`, `README-python-client.md` and the subcommand registry with #1607, #1581 and #1573.
